What causes burnout in healthcare? 6 key factors impacting clinicians today
summary: This blog post provides an overview about how burnout develops over time in clinical environments and its impact on clinicians and patients alike.
body_text: Organizational factors driving burnout in hospitals—such as alert fatigue, staffing constraints, and administrative burdens—continue to undermine employee well-being and organizational performance. Disorganized care coordination shows how burnout develops over time in clinical environments; centralizing communication, improving secure messaging, and enhancing access to EHR data help improve patient outcomes. Accurate on-call scheduling tools are essential for preventing burnout in healthcare while supporting stronger engagement and job fulfillment. Education and resources also play a critical role in minimizing clinician burnout by discouraging inefficient workarounds that disrupt workflows. Clinician burnout , defined as “a job-related stress syndrome resulting in emotional exhaustion, depersonalization, and reduced personal accomplishment,” is not a matter of motivation or resilience, but a complex issue in the medical landscape. While there has been encouraging momentum towards preventing burnout in healthcare, new findings from the State of Healthcare Communication report reveal a troubling trend: workplace stress increased by 89% compared to the previous year. Understanding the organizational factors driving burnout in hospitals requires a nuanced perspective. Differences in care delivery models, specialties, and patient populations mean that clinicians experience stress in various ways. By taking a closer look at how burnout develops over time in clinical environments, it’s easier to identify the causes and begin implementing meaningful strategies that better support care teams. Alert fatigue The noisy and fast-paced nature of hospitals makes it difficult for clinicians to focus and make the best decisions for their patients. Alert fatigue causes this sensory overload as care teams “become desensitized to safety alerts, and as a result ignore or fail to respond appropriately to such warnings.” For example, an intensive care unit ( ICU) study found that clinicians experience an average of 64.1 passive alerts per patient each day, but only 4.5% represent true panic values. These interruptions disrupt workflows and erode trust in critical notification systems. Over time, alert fatigue contributes to burnout in healthcare by affecting clinicians’ well-being and ultimately patient experiences. Hospitals and health systems are increasingly looking to enterprise alert management solutions that deliver secure, actionable notifications directly to the right clinician’s device. Reducing this unnecessary noise and minimizing overhead announcements are a few ways to address the key causes of clinician burnout. Poor care coordination Modern clinical environments require advanced and emerging technology to meet evolving patient needs. As a result, many areas of collaboration can hit roadblocks, exacerbating burnout in healthcare workers. These obstacles are not theoretical. The State of Healthcare Communications report found that adopting too many secure messaging platforms create haphazard workflows and impact employee confidence. Care teams are increasingly becoming comprehensive interprofessional groups, deepening the risks of clinician burnout. However, with more open communication, nurses report a lower association with workplace stress. A centralized communication system —combining secure messaging, alerts, paging, staff directories, and contact center functions—enhances coordination by reducing the number of individual tools that clinicians need to manage patient care. Staffing shortages The National Center for Health Workforce Analysis (NCHWA) projects that by 2038, there will be a shortage of registered nurses in cities, with 11% in suburban and rural areas. When hospitals are understaffed, the remaining nurses often take on heavier workloads, mandatory overtime, and back-to-back shifts that are correlated to greater burnout in healthcare. Staffing shortages can contribute to adverse events , intensifying clinician burnout. When nurse-to-patient ratios are too low, essential aspects of care are more likely to be missed, raising the risk of medication errors, patient falls, or even increased mortality. Equipping staff with effective tools, such as secure messaging , can help eliminate communication roadblocks that consume valuable time, allowing clinicians to devote more attention to patient care. Off-shift intrusions If hospitals rely on manual processes to create and update their on-call schedules, mistakes are bound to happen from human error. These outdated systems are worsened by healthcare organizations relying on HR information for their staff data, which may not accurately reflect how teams and departments are structured. The impact of inefficient clinical communication on staff burnout is evident in off-shift intrusions, where unnecessary calls, texts, or alerts reach clinicians when they’re not on duty. These disruptions limit time to rest and recharge, making it harder for them to return to work prepared for their patients. In fact, healthcare professionals who spend more time on EHR-related tasks outside of work are more likely to experience clinician burnout . Addressing this challenge requires implementing an on-call scheduling solution that routes up-to-date availability information, helping ensure communications are directed to the appropriate clinician at the appropriate time. Administrative burdens Today, 96% of hospitals rely on EHR systems designed to better organize patient information and improve its accuracy. At the same time, research suggests that EHRs have expanded administrative workloads and reshaped daily workflows; physicians are spending almost two hours on EHR and administrative work for every hour of clinical care. In another study , respondents reported that administrative tasks hindered their ability to provide high-quality care, shifting away from meaningful patient interactions and resulting in lower career satisfaction often seen with burnout in healthcare workers. By adopting communication tools that integrate with EHR data , alerts and orders are delivered with richer context, eliminating the need for clinicians to log into multiple systems or manually search for information. Lack of staff education Healthcare workers have varying levels of comfort with technology. If they aren’t confident using their tools—or inherit only partial knowledge from colleagues—they can become frustrated, losing time to trial-and-error and relying on workarounds. Over a third of healthcare workers (37%) already report feeling frustrated by their solutions, and nearly three in ten (28%) feel their organization doesn’t provide the necessary training to use them effectively. That’s why it’s paramount for organizations to provide education and resources, curated to specific roles and settings that are continuously updated as their solutions evolve and undergo product updates. With an estimated annual cost of $4.6 billion , burnout is a persistent challenge that needs to be addressed. As clinical environments become increasingly multifaceted, addressing them is more critical than ever. While technology alone can’t eliminate burnout, it plays a key role in supporting care teams and improving patient outcomes.

(“Treace” or the “Company”) (NasdaqGS: TMCI), a medical technology company driving a fundamental shift in the surgical treatment of bunions and related midfoot deformities, today announced the successful completion of the first cases utilizing its SuperBite™ Compression Screw System. SuperBite™ screws are engineered to deliver advanced compression through a variable thread pitch and optimized headless design, with its self-drilling and countersinking features enabling rapid screw insertion. The screw implants also incorporate a beveled head design with smoothed edges, making them ideal for both minimally invasive and traditional open surgical approaches. The SuperBite™ system offers comprehensive screw diameters ranging from 2.5mm to 7.0mm to address a broad range of foot & ankle surgical applications across the forefoot, midfoot, and hindfoot. Anne Holly Johnson, MD, of Hospital for Special Surgery (New York, New York) and a member of Treace’s Surgeon Advisory Board, performed the first cases with the new SuperBite™ screws. She commented, “My first cases with the SuperBite™ screws were very successful. I was impressed with the streamlined insertion and great compression. Compression screws are the most common fixation used in foot and ankle surgery, and I plan to use the SuperBite™ screws in many different fusion and osteotomy applications.” “The launch of SuperBite™ represents an important milestone in the expansion of our market-leading bunion & midfoot technology portfolio,” said John T. Treace, CEO and Chairman of Treace. “SuperBite™ allows our direct sales team to more fully service our 3,300+ surgeon customers technology needs, not only in the procedures they perform with us today, but also a significant volume of incremental procedures throughout the foot and ankle where compression screws are utilized. We believe SuperBite™ screws will expand our addressable market, accelerate our case volumes, and grow our customer share of wallet, all while further advancing our position as a 1-stop-shop for our customers.” Full commercialization of the SuperBite™ Compression Screw System is anticipated in the third quarter of 2026. Promoted to Region Vice President in 2019, he led his Texas region to win Region of the Year in 2020. In addition to promoting agent success, Neal has been instrumental in advancing Landstar’s safety initiatives by representing his region on multiple M.U.S.T. customer program visits. Landstar’s Mutual Understanding of Safety Together (M.U.S.T.) program brings Landstar agents and safety team members together with customers to collaborate on freight safety. Jeffrey C. Crowe-Robert E. Zonneville Lifetime Achievement Award Landstar Vice President, General Counsel, and Secretary Mike Kneller and Vice President of Government Services, Colonel Mike Cashner, U.S. Army, Retired, were both honored with the Jeffrey C. title: Polestar decouples growth from negative climate impact: emissions per sold car cut by 31% in five years
summary: Polestar (Nasdaq: PSNY) today publishes its 2025 Sustainability Report, showing how the Company has since 2020 reduced its GHG emissions per sold car by 31%.
body_text: “If you are not reducing emissions while growing, you are choosing not to,” says Michael Lohscheller, CEO Polestar Europe’s only pure EV company continues to deliver measurable progress instead of pledges, despite a volatile and challenged industry. Polestar 0 project: Large scale pilot for ultra-low-emission steel among progress GOTHENBURG, Sweden - 28 April 2026. Polestar (Nasdaq: PSNY) today publishes its 2025 Sustainability Report , showing how the Company has since 2020 reduced its GHG emissions per sold car by 31%. During the same period, Polestar has scaled its business and grown annual retail sales to over 60,000 cars, expanded across 28 markets, brought three new models to the road and established manufacturing in factories across three countries. As climate commitments slip across the car industry, policy signals waver and combustion engine investment continues, Polestar moves in the opposite direction: forward. Europe’s only pure EV company continues to deliver measurable progress instead of pledges, despite a volatile and challenged industry. The reduction in emissions per sold car since 2020 reflects the Company’s focus on increasing renewable energy use related to battery production and manufacturing, and use of low-carbon materials. Over the past year, increased volumes of Polestar 4, the company’s lowest carbon footprint car to date, has also been a significant factor, alongside the expansion of renewable energy across key European markets, which drives down use-phase emissions. Europe remains Polestar’s largest market, representing over 75% of sales. Polestar continues to stay below its emissions reduction curve, heading towards its goal of becoming a climate-neutral company by 2040. Michael Lohscheller, Polestar CEO, says: “If you are not reducing emissions while growing, you are choosing not to. Electrification delivers clear value for customers: lower running costs, lower emissions and greater peace of mind, as volatile oil prices and fuel scarcity mean pump anxiety is increasingly replacing range anxiety. As clean electricity scales, electric vehicles are becoming not just the sustainable choice, but the smarter, more reliable one.” At a societal level, electrification offers a clear path to reducing lifecycle GHG emissions from passenger transport, as renewable energy and EV adoption scale together. As electricity becomes cleaner and more stable than petroleum-based fuels, the role of electric vehicles as a climate solution is becoming even more evident. Recent results from the Polestar 0 project Work at the Mission 0 House in Gothenburg brings together industry and academia to eliminate emissions from high-impact materials, products, and processes. This research is driving new materials, technologies, and partnerships toward the Polestar 0 project goal of a net-zero car without offsets by 2035. The initial 2030 timeline has been revised, reflecting the scale and complexity of the challenge, but also the opportunity. On the contrary of giving up, Polestar consolidates the task through the dedicated research in the Mission 0 House. Fredrika Klarén, Head of Sustainability at Polestar, says: “The Polestar 0 project pushes us into new territory. While much of the industry invests in hybrids and combustion engines, we focus on solutions that eliminate emissions entirely. The innovation emerging from this project shows the power of collaboration and material science, and importantly, how well positioned we are to move the industry forward.” Key developments from Mission 0 House include: Large-scale pilot for ultra-low-emission steel Research on materials for batteries Development of bio-based textile alternatives Technologies converting CO₂ into new materials Mission 0 House was formally established in 2025, securing close to SEK 100 million in funding over five years towards the research consortium. The current collaboration includes five Swedish higher education institutions and six companies. Notes to editors Mission 0 House Since 2024, Polestar’s climate research is centered in Mission 0 House in Gothenburg, together with academia and different industries to eliminate emissions from materials, products, and processes. Following a pilot phase, Mission 0 House was formally established in 2025, securing close to SEK 100 million in funding. The aim is to develop scalable solutions and patents that support climate-neutral materials and products and help manufacturers reduce emissions. Research is organised across metals, chemicals, and processes, with interdisciplinary teams working closely together. During 2025, new partners joined and projects expanded, strengthening Mission 0 House as a platform for applied research and collaboration. The current collaboration includes five Swedish higher education institutions, University of Borås, University West, Jönköping University, Karlstad University, and Mid Sweden University, alongside companies Borgstena, Polestar, Sekab, SSAB, TMG Automotive, and Together Tech, with additional financial support from the Knowledge Foundation, Vinnova and Västra Götalandsregionen. Headquartered in Gothenburg, Sweden, its cars are available in 28 markets globally across North America, Europe and Asia Pacific. Polestar has four models in its line-up: Polestar 2, Polestar 3, Polestar 4, and Polestar 5. Planned models include the Polestar 7 compact SUV (to be introduced in 2028) and the Polestar 6 roadster. With its vehicles currently manufactured on two continents, North America and Asia, Polestar plans to diversify its manufacturing footprint further, with production of Polestar 7 planned in Europe. Polestar has an unwavering commitment to sustainability and has set an ambitious roadmap to reach its climate targets: halve greenhouse gas emissions by 2030 per-vehicle-sold and become climate-neutral across its value chain by 2040. Polestar’s comprehensive sustainability strategy covers the four areas of Climate, Transparency, Circularity, and Inclusion. body_text: What Processes can Improve Hardness and Elasticity? Heat treatment processes, especially aging, are highly effective for improving the hardness and elasticity of beryllium copper. During aging, the alloy is heated to a specific temperature and then slowly cooled, promoting the precipitation of beryllium in the copper matrix. This process significantly increases hardness and tensile strength, making the alloy more durable. Cold working, which involves deforming the material at room temperature, further enhances hardness and elasticity by increasing dislocation density and improving resistance to deformation. Solution treating and quenching produce a soft, ductile condition; hardness is developed later during aging. Dissolves into a solid solution; quenching creates a supersaturated structure for later precipitation hardening. The balance is achieved after subsequent aging, not during solution treatment alone. These treatments ensure that beryllium copper excels in high-stress, high-performance applications. Can Heat Treatment Significantly Increase Beryllium Copper Strength? Yes, properly applied heat treatment can increase beryllium copper's strength by 2 to 3 times compared to its annealed state. Through processes like aging and solution treating, the alloy changes its microstructure, significantly enhancing its strength. Aging, for instance, promotes the precipitation of beryllium in the copper matrix, resulting in a much harder and stronger material. This increase in strength allows beryllium copper to rival certain alloy steels in mechanical performance, making it suitable for high-stress applications. Despite the enhanced strength, beryllium copper retains its excellent electrical and thermal conductivity, making it versatile for use in industries like aerospace, electronics, and automotive, where both mechanical durability and efficient energy transfer are essential. What Tools are Commonly Made from Beryllium Copper Alloys? The Tools are commonly made from Beryllium Copper Alloys are listed below. Non-Sparking Tools: Beryllium copper is commonly used to make tools that require resistance to sparks, such as wrenches, pliers, and hammers. These tools are ideal for use in hazardous environments, such as in oil and gas or mining industries, where sparks could pose a risk of ignition. Precision Instruments: Beryllium copper alloys are used to manufacture precision instruments that require both strength and good electrical conductivity. Examples include gauges, measuring devices, and components in medical equipment, where accuracy and durability are critical. Molds and Dies: The alloy is frequently used for molds and dies in the manufacturing process, especially in injection molding and metal casting. Its high thermal conductivity helps in maintaining uniform heat distribution, which is essential for producing high-quality parts. Springs and Contacts: Beryllium copper is often used to create springs, electrical contacts, and connectors due to its excellent elasticity, strength, and electrical conductivity. These components are commonly used in electronics, telecommunications, and automotive industries. Electrical Connectors: Due to its excellent conductivity and strength, beryllium copper is often used in electrical connectors, switches, and relays. These are critical components in power transmission, automotive, and aerospace applications. Locking Mechanisms: Beryllium copper's strength and resistance to corrosion make it a popular choice for creating high-performance locking mechanisms. These are used in environments where reliability and resistance to wear are essential, such as in industrial machinery. Valve Components: The alloy is also used to make valve components, including valve seats, stems, and springs. These parts benefit from beryllium copper's excellent corrosion resistance and ability to withstand high pressures and temperatures. Aerospace Components: In the aerospace industry, beryllium copper is used for making parts such as actuators, bushings, and bearings due to its combination of high strength, wear resistance, and ability to withstand extreme conditions. Why are Beryllium Copper Tools Preferred in Hazardous or Sensitive Environments? Beryllium copper tools are preferred in hazardous or sensitive environments because they are non-sparking and non-magnetic, reducing the risk of ignition or interference with sensitive equipment. The non-sparking property makes them ideal for use in industries such as oil and gas, mining, and chemical processing, where even a small spark can lead to dangerous explosions or fires. Beryllium copper tools are also resistant to corrosion, ensuring long-lasting performance even in harsh, high-moisture, or chemically active environments. The strength and durability of beryllium copper further contribute to its preference in these environments. The tools can withstand mechanical stress, impact, and abrasion, making them suitable for heavy-duty applications. Despite their high strength, they retain good electrical and thermal conductivity, essential for tasks involving electrical connections, temperature regulation, or precision work. The combination of these properties ensures that beryllium copper tools perform reliably and safely in both hazardous and sensitive environments, where safety and durability are critical. Are Beryllium Copper Tools Spark Resistant? Yes, beryllium copper is inherently non-sparking due to the alloy’s composition and properties. The addition of beryllium to copper creates an alloy that significantly reduces the likelihood of sparking when struck or scraped against hard surfaces. However, it is important to note that while beryllium copper is non-sparking, it may still produce micro-sparks under specific high-stress conditions, particularly at high velocities or when interacting with certain materials. This makes it a safe option in environments where sparks can ignite flammable substances. The non-sparking characteristic makes beryllium copper a standard choice in industries (mining, oil, chemical, and other hazardous sectors), where spark prevention is critical for ensuring worker safety and preventing potential explosions. The material’s durability and resistance to wear enhance its suitability for high-risk environments where tools are subjected to constant impact or friction. What are the Uses of Beryllium Copper The uses of Beryllium Copper are listed below. Electrical Components: Beryllium copper is widely used in electrical applications such as connectors, relays, and electrical contacts. Its excellent electrical conductivity and durability make it ideal for components that require both mechanical strength and the ability to conduct electricity. Precision Tools: Due to its high strength and non-sparking properties, beryllium copper is commonly used to make precision tools, including wrenches, pliers, and hammers. These tools are essential in hazardous environments, such as oil rigs and chemical plants, where sparks could ignite dangerous materials. Aerospace and Military Parts: Beryllium copper is used in the aerospace and military industries to create parts that require both strength and conductivity, such as actuators, springs, and bushings. Its resistance to corrosion and ability to perform under extreme conditions make it suitable for these applications. Molds and Dies: The alloy is used to make molds and dies in manufacturing processes like injection molding and die-casting. Beryllium copper’s high thermal conductivity ensures uniform heat distribution, which is essential for producing high-quality parts. Automotive Components: Beryllium copper is used in automotive applications, including electrical contacts and sensors, where its combination of conductivity and durability ensures reliable performance in challenging environments. Springs and Valves: Due to its high elasticity and strength, beryllium copper is used to manufacture springs, valves, and other components subjected to mechanical stress. These parts are found in various industries, including industrial machinery and medical devices. Sparking-resistant tools: Beryllium copper tools are essential in explosive or flammable environments because they are non-sparking. They are commonly used in environments such as mining, oil exploration, and chemical processing, where safety is a priority. How Does Beryllium Copper Compare to Alloy Steel and Carbon Steel? Beryllium copper is stronger than many copper alloys and some low-carbon steels, but most carbon steels (especially medium/high-carbon and hardened steels) exceed it in strength and hardness. Unlike alloy steel and carbon steel, beryllium copper maintains excellent electrical and thermal conductivity, making it ideal for electrical components. While alloy steel is generally stronger and more durable, especially in high-temperature applications, it lacks the conductivity of beryllium copper. Carbon steel is typically stronger and harder than beryllium copper (depending on grade), but lacks conductivity. Beryllium copper is preferred when both mechanical properties and conductivity are needed, advantages not simultaneously offered by alloy steel and carbon steel . What Mechanical Properties Differentiate Beryllium Copper from Steel Alloys? Beryllium copper differs from steel alloys in several mechanical properties. While steel alloys, particularly alloy and carbon steels, offer higher strength and hardness, beryllium copper maintains excellent elasticity, allowing it to return to its original shape after deformation. Beryllium copper is also more corrosion-resistant than steel, making it suitable for harsh environments. Unlike many steel alloys, which are relatively poor conductors of electricity, beryllium copper excels in both electrical and thermal conductivity, making it highly suitable for applications in electronics and other industries requiring efficient heat and electrical transfer. Many steel alloys offer higher strength and hardness than beryllium copper, while beryllium copper exhibits high elasticity and good fatigue resistance; however, both materials can exhibit elastic behavior within their limits. Is Beryllium Copper More Corrosion Resistant Than Carbon Steel? Yes, beryllium copper is more corrosion-resistant than carbon steel. Beryllium copper’s composition allows it to perform well in harsh environments, including exposure to moisture, chemicals, and moderate to high temperatures. However, extreme conditions, such as exposure to high heat for prolonged periods or aggressive chemical environments, can still cause some degradation over time. In contrast, carbon steel is highly susceptible to rust and corrosion unless coated or treated. Beryllium copper’s resistance to oxidation and its ability to perform well in corrosive conditions make it ideal for use in industries like aerospace, marine, and electronics, where long-lasting durability is required in demanding environments. How Does Beryllium Copper Compare with Other Copper Alloys? Beryllium copper generally has higher strength and hardness than most copper alloys while retaining moderate electrical and thermal conductivity (lower than pure copper but higher than many high-strength alloys). Brass and bronze are alloyed for a range of properties (strength, corrosion resistance, wear resistance, castability, and machinability), not solely machinability or cost. It is especially suited for applications requiring non-sparking, such as in hazardous environments. Beryllium copper's ability to maintain its electrical and thermal conductivity while being significantly stronger than other copper alloys makes it ideal for precision tools, electrical contacts, and aerospace components where both mechanical performance and conductivity are essential. What Advantages Does BeCu Offer Over Brass or Bronze? The advantages that BeCu offers over Brass or Bronze are listed below. Higher Strength and Hardness: Beryllium copper (BeCu) offers significantly higher strength and hardness compared to brass and bronze, making it ideal for heavy-duty applications requiring durable, wear-resistant materials. Improved Corrosion Resistance: Beryllium copper is more resistant to corrosion than brass and bronze, especially in harsh environments, including exposure to moisture, chemicals, and high temperatures. This makes it more suitable for applications in aerospace, marine, and other demanding industries. Non-Sparking Properties: Unlike brass and bronze, BeCu is non-sparking, making it essential for use in hazardous environments such as oil rigs, chemical plants, and mining operations, where sparks could cause explosions or fires. Maintains Electrical and Thermal Conductivity: While both brass and bronze provide some level of conductivity, beryllium copper retains excellent electrical and thermal conductivity, making it ideal for electrical components and heat-sensitive applications. Enhanced Fatigue Resistance: BeCu exhibits superior fatigue resistance compared to brass and bronze, allowing it to perform well under repeated mechanical stress, making it suitable for precision tools, springs, and other critical components. Higher Elasticity: Beryllium copper has superior elasticity compared to brass and bronze, making it ideal for creating springs and other components that need to return to their original shape after being deformed. Better Wear Resistance: Due to its higher hardness and toughness, BeCu exhibits better wear resistance than brass or bronze, which leads to a longer lifespan of tools, parts, and components exposed to friction. Precision Machinability: While brass and bronze are easier to machine, BeCu still allows for precision machining due to its excellent balance of hardness and ductility. It can be molded and machined into intricate shapes without compromising its strength and durability. Higher Performance in High-Temperature Applications: BeCu Beryllium copper performs better at higher temperatures compared to brass and bronze, but some bronzes and steels perform better at elevated temperatures, depending on the application. This makes it suitable for high-performance applications in environments where other alloys might have limitations, often seen in brass and bronze. Does Beryllium Copper Outperform Brass in Strength and Durability? Yes, beryllium copper outperforms brass in both strength and durability. Beryllium copper is significantly stronger than brass, with its tensile strength and hardness being much higher, especially after heat treatment. The addition of beryllium to copper increases its strength by up to 3 times compared to pure annealed copper, significantly enhancing its resistance to wear, deformation, and mechanical stress. This enhanced strength makes beryllium copper more suitable for applications where high durability is required, such as in precision tools, aerospace components, and electrical connectors. Beryllium copper offers superior fatigue resistance, enabling it to withstand repeated mechanical stress without failure, a performance not consistently achieved by brass. Brass provides durability and corrosion resistance, yet its overall strength and ability to endure high-stress conditions fall short compared to beryllium copper. Beryllium copper is often preferred in demanding environments requiring high strength and fatigue resistance, though some bronzes (e.g., aluminum bronze) may match or exceed it in specific applications. How is Beryllium Copper Used in Die Casting? Beryllium copper is primarily used as a die material (tooling/inserts) in die casting, not commonly as the cast metal itself, particularly when strength and conductivity are important. In the die casting process, molten metals such as aluminum, zinc, or magnesium are injected into molds; beryllium copper is used for mold components (e.g., inserts, cores) due to thermal conductivity, allowing for the production of intricate parts with excellent surface finish and dimensional accuracy. The high strength and wear resistance of beryllium copper make it ideal for producing tools and components subjected to mechanical stress, such as connectors and electrical components. The alloy's high thermal conductivity is especially beneficial in die casting, as it helps in maintaining uniform temperature during the molding process, leading to better-quality castings with fewer defects. Moreover, beryllium copper's ability to withstand high temperatures and pressures without degrading makes it well-suited for producing parts that will be used in demanding environments, such as automotive, aerospace, and electronic industries. Beryllium copper die-castings are known for their long lifespan, resistance to corrosion, and consistent performance, making them a reliable choice for high-performance applications. What Advantages does Beryllium Copper Offer in Die Cast Components? The advantages that Beryllium Copper offers in die-cast components are listed below. High Strength and Durability: Beryllium copper offers high strength and durability when used as die material (inserts/tooling), improving tool life and performance, making die-cast more resistant to wear and mechanical stress. This makes it ideal for high-performance parts that need to endure heavy use over time. Excellent Thermal Conductivity: The high thermal conductivity of beryllium copper helps in maintaining uniform temperature during the die-casting process. This results in better quality castings with fewer defects, making the production process more efficient and reliable. Superior Corrosion Resistance: Corrosion resistance applies to BeCu tooling; die-cast components are typically aluminum, zinc, or magnesium alloys, which makes it suitable for die-cast components exposed to moisture, chemicals, and harsh environments, ensuring longer-lasting durability and reducing maintenance needs. Non-Sparking Properties: Beryllium copper's non-sparking characteristic makes it ideal for die-cast tools used in explosive or flammable environments, such as in mining or chemical processing, where spark prevention is critical for safety. Precision and Detail: Die casting using BeCu inserts improves precision and detail due to better thermal control and reduced distortion. The alloy’s combination of strength and ductility makes it ideal for producing precision parts in industries like aerospace and electronics. High-Temperature Performance: Beryllium copper maintains its strength and hardness at high temperatures, which is crucial for die-cast components used in high-heat applications such as automotive and industrial machinery. Improved Fatigue Resistance: Beryllium copper’s ability to withstand repeated mechanical stress without cracking or breaking makes it an excellent choice for components that will undergo constant movement or load, such as springs and connectors. Enhanced Wear Resistance: The high hardness of beryllium copper provides superior wear resistance, reducing the frequency of replacement and ensuring a longer service life for die-cast components exposed to friction, such as gears or bushings. Can Beryllium Copper Improve Precision in Die Casting? Yes, beryllium copper can improve precision in die casting when used as die/tooling material (inserts), not as the cast metal itself. The strength and ductility of BeCu improve tool durability and stability, which supports the consistent production of intricate shapes, which are essential in industries requiring high-precision parts, such as aerospace and electronics. Beryllium copper has high thermal conductivity (though lower than pure copper) and is significantly higher than tool steels used in dies. Thermal conductivity is a primary advantage in die casting, enabling rapid heat removal, reduced cycle time, and improved dimensional stability. What Makes Beryllium Copper a Valuable Metal? Beryllium copper is a valuable metal due to its unique combination of properties, which make it suitable for a wide range of applications. Its high strength allows it to withstand heavy mechanical stress, while its excellent electrical and thermal conductivity make it ideal for electrical components. The alloy also offers good corrosion resistance, performing well in many environments, particularly in non-oxidizing or mildly corrosive conditions, ensuring durability even in harsh environments. Furthermore, beryllium copper is non-sparking, which makes it a critical material for use in hazardous industries. Its balance of strength, conductivity, and resistance to wear and corrosion makes it highly versatile and valuable across industries like aerospace, electronics, and automotive. How Do Its Properties Benefit Electrical and Mechanical Uses? Beryllium copper’s properties provide significant benefits in both electrical and mechanical applications. Its excellent electrical conductivity makes it ideal for use in electrical contacts, connectors, and switches, where efficient power transfer is crucial. In mechanical applications, its high strength and durability ensure that components can withstand heavy stress without failing, making it perfect for tools, precision instruments, and aerospace components. Beryllium copper offers good corrosion resistance, but it is not as resistant as some other specialized alloys, like stainless steel, in extremely harsh environments. Additionally, its elasticity and non-sparking nature make it suitable for use in applications where both mechanical performance and safety are paramount. Is Beryllium Copper Non Ferrous? Yes, beryllium copper is a non-ferrous metal. Unlike ferrous metals, which contain iron as a primary component, beryllium copper is primarily composed of copper with small amounts of beryllium. The absence of iron in beryllium copper contributes to its non-ferrous nature, which provides non-magnetic properties and contributes to corrosion resistance. However, its weight is comparable to that of copper alloys, not significantly lighter than all ferrous metals. As a non-ferrous metal, beryllium copper is especially valuable in applications where these properties are critical, such as in electrical components, aerospace parts, and medical devices. How Are Non Ferrous Metals Like Beryllium Copper Used in Industry? Non-ferrous metals like beryllium copper are widely used in industries requiring high strength, durability, and excellent electrical and thermal conductivity. In aerospace, beryllium copper is used for components such as connectors, actuators, and bushings, offering both mechanical strength and conductivity. It is also crucial in oil and gas, chemical processing, and mining industries due to its non-sparking properties, which make it safe in hazardous environments. In electronics, beryllium copper is used for connectors, switches, and relays due to its corrosion resistance and conductivity. The automotive industry relies on it for brake components, valve springs, and sensors, where high performance and durability are essential. Its combination of strength, conductivity, and resistance to wear also makes it valuable for precision tools, springs, and medical devices, ensuring reliability in critical applications, further reinforcing its importance among Non‑Ferrous Metals. What Applications Take Advantage of Non Ferrous Properties? Non-ferrous metals like beryllium copper are essential in a variety of applications that require materials with high strength, corrosion resistance, and good electrical and thermal conductivity. Industries such as aerospace, electronics, and automotive take advantage of these properties. Beryllium copper’s non-ferrous nature significantly reduces the risk of rust or corrosion compared to ferrous metals, making it ideal for components exposed to harsh environments. However, it is important to note that beryllium copper may still experience some degradation in highly aggressive environments, particularly under extreme chemical exposure. Additionally, its non-magnetic and non-sparking characteristics are crucial in industries dealing with explosive or flammable materials, such as oil and gas and chemical processing, where safety is a top priority. In medical and scientific instruments, non-ferrous metals like beryllium copper are used for components that require precise performance and long-term reliability, such as surgical tools and MRI machine parts. Marine applications also benefit from the corrosion resistance of non-ferrous metals, especially for marine fasteners and components that need to endure saltwater exposure without degrading. In telecommunications, electricity transmission systems, and solar panels, non-ferrous metals are preferred for their high conductivity and ability to maintain performance in extreme conditions. Can Beryllium Copper Resist Corrosion Better Than Steel? Yes, beryllium copper offers superior corrosion resistance compared to many steels, especially in environments exposed to moisture, chemicals, and high temperatures. Beryllium copper has excellent resistance to oxidation and corrosion, maintaining its strength and appearance even under harsh conditions. Steel, particularly carbon steel, is highly susceptible to rust and corrosion unless it is coated or treated with anti-corrosive substances. In contrast, beryllium copper maintains its strength and appearance even under harsh conditions, making it more durable and reliable for applications in industries like aerospace, marine, and electronics. Its corrosion resistance is one of the key reasons it is preferred for critical components in such demanding environments.

title: Slash raises $100M Series C at a $1.4B valuation
summary: Led by Ribbit Capital, Goodwater Capital, and Khosla Ventures to bring a higher standard of business finance to every business.
body_text: At Slash, we believe your bank account should do more . It shouldn’t just be the place you hold your money, it should be your business’ financial command center.¹ One place to: Find and eliminate wasteful spend. Accept payments and invoice your customers. Automate your accounting busywork. Understand your finances in real time. And much more. Today, we’re announcing a $100 million Series C at a $1.4 billion valuation, bringing our total funding to $160 million. We’re excited to bring on Ribbit Capital as our lead investor in the round, and to have Khosla Ventures and Goodwater Capital co-leading. Goodwater, who led our Series B just 16 months ago, is doubling down. NEA and YC are investing in Slash for a fourth time. This fundraise is a testament to the incredible amount of time and quality of work the entire team at Slash has put in over the course of the last 5 years. We can’t wait to use these resources to deliver immense value to our customers. It’s been a grind I started Slash at 18, in the middle of the pandemic. Itching to start a business, I convinced the smartest engineer I knew – my co-founder Kevin – to take a break from school and come live in LA with me. We didn’t know exactly what we were building yet, but we knew we wanted to build something meaningful. A few pivots into our journey, we met our current Head of Customer Success, Brenden Truong. Brenden taught us all about the sneaker resale space, where we first found product-market fit. Within a year, we had scaled to $5M in ARR and raised a Series A. Then the market disappeared. What had been our entire growth engine collapsed almost overnight. This was both the toughest moment for me as a founder, and the best thing that ever happened to Slash. It forced us to think bigger. What larger industry could we go after? How could we deliver differentiated value to businesses in many industries simultaneously? After all, every business owner in the world needs a bank account. The question was, how could we build a better one? The Slash Thesis The answer was simple: do more . Legacy banks are static, rigid, and one-size-fits-all. Businesses aren’t. Marketing agencies want to segment spend by client, so we built virtual accounts. Wholesalers want to transact in stablecoins, so we built stablecoin payments.⁴ The list goes on. Your bank account should adapt to your business, not the other way around. From day one, we’ve built by listening closely to our customers and shipping the tools they actually need, especially the ones no one else is willing to build. That approach has compounded. Every industry we serve makes the product better for all the rest — and that flywheel only accelerates. Today, Slash processes: We inflected in 2025 For most of our history, Slash was focused on a handful of verticals. That changed in 2025. We reached a point where we had built enough product depth and earned enough trust, that Slash became broadly useful across industries. Now, our growth is accelerating on top of our scale . In Q1 2026, Slash’s growth accelerated, with total purchase volume and revenue increasing faster quarter over quarter than it did over the same period in 2025, on a much larger base. This is hard to do, but it’s because we’re shipping product faster than anyone else. In the last 12 months alone, we launched over 100 features. These include: A new mobile app Global USD (Slash for non US businesses)³ Expense management and reimbursements Accounting Automation Invoicing Real Time Payments API Today, we serve more than 5,000 ambitious companies across a variety of industries — from tech startups like Bland and DualEntry , to gaming companies like Triumph , large HVAC companies, e-commerce brands like Nectar and Hike Footwear , and a range of small businesses — who rely on Slash to operate at their best. AI is only going to let us go faster We are shipping an order of magnitude faster in early 2026 than we were in 2025. By the end of the year, Slash will run your financial back office for you. Every waking second of a business owner’s time should be spent on the needle moving parts of their business: not their finances, not accounting busywork. If you manage a business and want to experience banking that goes above and beyond, take a demo of Slash . We’d love to work with you. And if you are someone who wants to join one of America’s fastest growing companies and help us build this generation’s most consequential financial services business, please visit our careers page. We are just getting started.
